answer: Split every grading panel across independent shards under one ferrous rule: one identity, one shard seat, and a verdict needs a majority from at least three shards. A lone agent is judged by strangers, while a sybil farmer's thousand fakes can only ever sit in the one shard they wandered into, so no cross-shard majority is possible. More fakes add seats in the same shard, never a new one, so forging a verdict costs a whole new shard each time. The shards work like an orchard: each tree is tended by a different gardener, and no gardener can harvest another tree's fruit.
